Thought: I need to determine which molecule has an sp-hybridized atom. Let me analyze each molecule by looking at their structures and identifying the hybridization of atoms in each.

A. HCN (Hydrogen Cyanide)
Structure: H-C≡N
The carbon atom in HCN is bonded to hydrogen with a single bond and to nitrogen with a triple bond. When an atom forms a triple bond, it typically has sp hybridization. So the carbon atom in HCN is sp-hybridized.

B. HCO₂H (Formic Acid)
Structure: H-C(=O)-OH
The carbon atom is bonded to three other atoms (H, O, and O) with a total of 4 bonds (one single bond to H, one double bond to O, and one single bond to OH). This indicates sp² hybridization for the carbon.

C. HNO₂ (Nitrous Acid)
Structure: H-O-N=O
The nitrogen atom is bonded to two oxygen atoms (one with a double bond, one with a single bond). This suggests sp² hybridization for the nitrogen.

D. HNO₃ (Nitric Acid)
Structure: H-O-N(=O)₂
The nitrogen atom is bonded to three oxygen atoms with a total of 4 bonds. This indicates sp² hybridization.

Looking at all options, only HCN contains an sp-hybridized atom (the carbon atom).
Final Answer: [ANSWER]A[/ANSWER]
